entry.title: Understanding the New API Rate Limit Headers in SAP SuccessFactors (with a Real Response Example)
entry.content:
Introduction

With the 2608 release (17 August 2026), SAP SuccessFactors began applying soft rate limits to all existing tenants, as part of the new SAP API Policy. Nothing is blocked yet, but every API response now carries standardized rate limit headers. SAP will later convert these soft limits to hard limits, and requests that exceed a hard limit will be rejected with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). SAP has not announced a date for that conversion, and new public APIs launched from 13 November 2026 will already be hard-limited.

API Rate Limit :

1. What is changing

Who Limit type When
All existing tenantsSoft (observed and flagged, not blocked)Since 2608 (17 Aug 2026)
New public APIsHard (HTTP 429)From 13 Nov 2026
Tenants provisioned on/after 1 Jan 2027HardFrom day one
Existing tenants, all APIsSoft converted to hardDate to be announced by SAP

Hard limits that were already set for specific tenants before this announcement stay in force. Limits apply at two scopes, and a request must satisfy both:

  • Resource level: per endpoint, and checked first.
  • Tenant level: shared by all integrations and users in the tenant, and checked second.

There are no per-user or per-integration limits, so one noisy integration can consume budget that other integrations need. Integration Center jobs and other internal SuccessFactors calls don't count, but SAP Integration Suite (BTP), middleware and custom apps do.

2. Reading the headers: a real example

I called the OData v2 entity BenefitEmployeeClaim with a plain GET request from Postman. The call returned 200 OK, and the response headers contained the following:

The two headers work as a pair. Ratelimit-Policy describes the rules, and Ratelimit shows where you currently stand.

 

Parameter Meaning
qQuota: the number of requests allowed in the window
wWindow length in seconds
mEnforcement mode (soft or hard)
rRequests remaining in the current window
tSeconds until the window resets

Interpreting this response:

  • customized-spike-arrest: 75 requests per 60 seconds, mode soft. There are 73 requests remaining and the counter resets in 26 seconds. In other words, 2 requests have been counted in this window.
  • tenant-quota: 600 requests per 60 seconds for the whole tenant. There are 598 remaining. (The enforcement mode is cut off in my screenshot, so check it in your own response.)

Two things are worth noting. First, the spike-arrest quota here (75/min) differs from the 25/min used in the example in SAP's KBA, so limits clearly vary by resource, and you shouldn't assume a single number. Second, in a hard-mode 429 response, the policy where r=0 is the one that was violated, and you can cross-reference it with Ratelimit-Policy to see its quota, window and mode.

3. What you should do now

  1. Start monitoring. Log the Ratelimit-Policy and Ratelimit headers in your middleware or API client. This is the best way to find out which integrations are close to their limits before enforcement begins.
  2. Add 429 handling now. On a 429, don't retry immediately. Honor the Retry-After header, use exponential backoff (for example 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s) with random jitter, and log every 429 as an integration health signal.
  3. Reduce unnecessary calls. Batch requests where possible, cache reference data such as picklists, pull only records changed since the last run, and stagger scheduled jobs instead of starting them all on the hour.
  4. Leave headroom. Design for roughly 70–80% of the limit under normal load, so retries and peaks don't push you over.
  5. Plan for go-lives. SAP has confirmed an exemption process with an expiry date for go-live, hypercare and peak periods. You request it by logging a case under component LOD-SF-INT-API.

 

 

Soft limits give you a grace period. Every SuccessFactors API response already tells you which policies apply to it, how much budget is left and when it resets. Use that period to find your heaviest integrations, add proper 429 handling and bring call volumes down. When SAP announces the move to hard limits, integrations that already monitor the headers and back off correctly shouldn't notice a difference.

For the complete list of endpoint-specific limits (92+ endpoints), see the Rate Limits page in the SAP SuccessFactors API Reference Guide (OData V2) on SAP Help Portal.

References

  • SAP Note 3792944, FAQ: API Rate Limits for SAP SuccessFactors
  • SAP Help Portal, SAP SuccessFactors API Reference Guide (OData V2), Rate Limits

entry.title: Deploying SAP SmartRecruiters Without SuccessFactors Employee Central
entry.content:
One of the most common questions we get from account teams and CSMs: "Can a customer go live on SmartRecruiters without Employee Central?"
The short answer is yes. But the right answer is: yes, with trade-offs you need to understand before the contract is signed.
This post is a reusable field guide ,  built from real delivery conversations, for anyone supporting a standalone SR deployment.

Bookmark it, share it with your SR SPOCs, and use it in deal reviews.

 

1. SR Without EC: What Works, What Doesn't

SmartRecruiters has no hard dependency on SAP ERP, S/4HANA, or legacy SF Recruiting. The deployment is clean. But without Employee Central, several productized capabilities are simply off the table:

  • No Master Data Sync: Foundation Objects (Legal Entity, Department, Cost Center, Location, Job Classification) live in EC. Without it, org fields in SR must be loaded manually or via API.
  • No Position-Led Hiring: SF Position Management is an EC sub-module. Without it, jobs are created manually inside SR.
  • No standard Hire Handoff: The productized sync pushes hired candidates to EC Manage Pending Hires. Without EC, a custom integration back to ECC/S/4HANA is required for employee record creation.

Bottom line: SR is a fully functional ATS standalone. But the end-to-end productized SAP ↔ SR pipeline is only available once EC is in scope.

Key question every account team should ask: Is EC on the customer's S/4HANA transformation roadmap? If yes, sequence SR deployment to avoid rebuilding org field mappings when EC goes live.

 

2. User Management & SSO: The Non-Negotiables

Regardless of whether EC is licensed, the SSO and user management architecture is fixed.

Layer

Requirement

IAS (Identity Authentication Service)

Always required as it powers SSO between SF and SR

SSO path

SF → IAS → SR (users navigate via the SF module picker)

User Sync

Users must exist in SF (BizX platform) first → hourly sync to SR

MFA

Mandatory as of June 18, 2026 for email/password login. Applies to the first provisioning admin only. All others log in via SSO.

Without EC

Users managed in the SF Platform shell, manually or via bulk import. No automated user lifecycle.

 

Two risks to flag early:

  • SR supports only one IdP: multiple Azure AD / Entra tenants is a blocker to surface before architecture is set.
  • Consultants and admins each need an SF user account + IAS account + correct RBP configuration.

 

3. BizX Tenant Provisioning: Get This Right at Booking

Under SKU 8020811 (SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors), provisioning depends on whether EC is licensed.

Without EC:

Reference: SAP Standard Tenant Provisioning Specification Sheet (SAP Trust Center): sap.com/docs/download/agreements/product-policy/css/service-specifications/sap-successfactors-standard-tenant-provisioning-scope-english-v7-2026a.pdf

 

Operational must-knows:

  • Even without EC, BizX tenants are provisioned : they host IAS, user management, and the SF module picker.
  • 10-day SLA from contract signature to start date: flag this the moment a go-live date is discussed.
  • At ordering: select the entitlement set that includes the customer's existing BizX tenant.
  • Recruiting Marketing must be provisioned in SAP to enable Career Site Builder: add this to the provisioning request.

 

4. Four Decisions That Must Happen in Week 1

These have long-tail consequences. Don't leave them for later:

  • Get EC on the S/4HANA roadmap: Even lightweight EC unlocks the full productized pipeline and avoids a post-migration rebuild.
  • Design the hire handoff to ECC/S/4 on day one: This is a custom integration, not productized. Don't discover it mid-build.
  • Let ECC/S/4 stabilize before finalizing SR org fields: Any HR system field change forces a rebuild in SR.
  • Scope Candidate Messaging (SMS/WhatsApp) countries early: 3–7 weeks lead time depending on channels.

 

Important: THR104 certification is mandatory for anyone (partner or customer) implementing

entry.title: Introducing Organizational Modeling in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central
entry.content:
Picture this — your organization is expanding into a new market. Leadership is aligned, the strategy is set, and now HR needs to make it happen. A new organizational unit needs to be created, departments need to move, positions need to realign, and everyone has an opinion on how the structure should look. You are individually coordinating with stakeholders; using spreadsheets, PowerPoints, disconnected tools to plan and model the change — and when the decision is finally made, you need to manually execute these changes in the system hoping nothing gets missed. Sound familiar? 

This is the reality for many HR teams today. Organizational change is constant, but the tools to manage it confidently have not always kept pace. The result is manual effort, misaligned data, and delayed decisions made without a clear picture of the full impact. 

That changes with SAP SuccessFactors Organizational Modeling. Available with the SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 Release, this new integrated capability gives HR and business leaders a centralized, controlled environment to plan, model, and visualize organizational changes before they are implemented, and to automatically apply the changes directly to their live SAP SuccessFactors environment. SAP SuccessFactors Organizational Modeling is a solution built on SAP BTP and is included with your Employee Central subscription at no additional cost.

What you can do with Organizational Modeling 

Key capabilities

  • Complete project context in one place — Capture the business rationale, effective date, supporting attachments, and project title translations in one centralized workspace, giving everyone involved full visibility into the purpose and scope of the organizational change. 
  • Stakeholder collaboration — Add project team members, assign roles, and control whether they can edit or view — ensuring the right stakeholders are involved at the right level without compromising the integrity of the process. 
  • Intuitive visualization — Use Chart view for drag-and-drop moves and List view for bulk position moves, with seamless switching between views. 
  • Scenario-based planning — Create multiple what-if simulations of future organizational structures before any change is applied to the live system. 
  • Validation before submission — Detect structural inconsistencies and errors before changes go live. 
  • Automated cascading updates — When a change is approved and submitted, the system automatically cascades updates across all related organizational objects and employee job information. This eliminates manual updates for individual object type and reduces the risk of errors. 
  • Role-based access control — Access is managed through a combination of SAP SuccessFactors Role-Based Permissions and authorization groups in SAP Cloud Identity Services, ensuring only authorized users can view, model, and publish organizational changes. 

Supported organizational objects: 

  • Legal Entity
  • Business Unit 
  • Division 
  • Department 
  • Cost Center
  • Position 

Operations Supported in the 2H 2026 Release: 

  • Create and delete new org units 
  • Deactivate existing org units 
  • Move org units and positions within the hierarchy 
  • Edit org units 

What you need to get started 

Prerequisites 

To fully leverage Organizational Modeling, your organization must have a strong Employee Central foundation with Position Management in use (with Position-to-Job Information synchronization configured).

Steps to setup SAP SuccessFactors Organizational Modeling 

We understand you may have questions and we are here to support you through this introduction. Here are the recommended next steps: 

Step 1 — Submit a provisioning request through SAP for Me 

Enable Organizational Modeling for your SAP SuccessFactors environment. Submit separate requests via SAP for Me for your Preview and Production environments.  

Please Note: if your data center is not provisioned yet, please allow up to 20 days for enablement. 

Step 2 — Configure permissions in both systems 

Assign the required Role-Based Permissions in SAP SuccessFactors and the corresponding authorization groups in SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS). Ensure user assignments are aligned consistently across both systems before onboarding begins. Both configurations are required — configuring only one results in incomplete access. 

User Type  

SAP BTP - IAS Groups  

SAP SF Permission  

All Users  

Org Modeling User  

Administrator Permissions -> Organizational Modeling -> Access Organizational Modeling  

System Administrator  

Org Modeling System Admin  

Miscellaneous Permissions → Organizational Modeling Configuration  

Project Creators  

Org Modeling Project Creator  

 

Project Administrators  

Org Modeling Project Admin  

 

Change Publishers  

Org Modeling Change Publisher  

Administrator Permissions -> Organizational Modeling -> Submit Organizational Modeling Projects 

Step 3 — Replicate Organizational Objects from SAP SuccessFactors to Organizational Modeling

Replicate the organizational object data from SAP SuccessFactors to the Organizational Modeling application by following the process below

1. Create the OrganizationalModelingConfiguration object in SAP SuccessFactors

Go to Manage Data within SAP SuccessFactors, create a new OrganizationalModelingConfiguration object and select the organizational objects your organization uses (Business Unit, Legal Entity, Division, Department, Cost Center, Position). 

2. Complete the guided onboarding process in Organizational Modeling

After the OrganizationalModelingConfiguration is created, the Org Modeling System Admin must complete a guided three-step onboarding process in Admin Center (within Organizational Modeling): configuration check, initial data replication, and org structure configuration. Choose Complete Onboarding to activate the application.

Create Organizational Modeling Projects

After the administrator completes the above setup steps, users responsible for project creation can begin creating Organizational Modeling projects.

Please Note: For detailed guidance refer to 'Setting up Organizational Modeling' in the SAP Help Portal link provided below in the 'Learn more with additional resources' section. 

What's coming next* 

The following capabilities are planned for 1H 2027* and beyond: 

  • Approval workflows — Ensure every change is reviewed by the right stakeholders before implementation. 
  • Conflict resolution — Include or exclude live organizational changes during your simulation to avoid conflicts. 
  • Cross-org movements — Model restructures across business units and board areas in a single exercise. 
  • Position hierarchy updates — Automatically realign reporting relationships when organizational units move. 
  • Organizational Modeling Agent — An intelligent organizational design optimization experience providing organizational health analysis, automated design proposals aligned with target KPIs, and insights into impacts and trade-offs. 

*As typical of any roadmap item, the information stated above is based on current information, may be changed by SAP at any time without notice, and should not influence your future purchasing decisions. Please subscribe to this blog to stay up to date.

Learn more with additional resources 

Comprehensive resources are available to support your adoption of SAP SuccessFactors Organizational Modeling: 

  • SAP Help Portal — Setup and configuration guides for Organizational Modeling in Employee Central: Implementing and Managing Organizational Modeling in Employee Central 
  • What's New Viewer — Track the latest releases and feature updates for Organizational Modeling. - Organizational Modeling in Employee Central  

Have a Question? 

For questions regarding this feature, please leave a comment below. 

Need Support? 

If you encounter any issues while setting up or testing Organizational Modeling, please create an incident with the component LOD-SF-EC-OMD.

entry.title: Automating Employee Contract Extension Based on Contract End Date in SAP SuccessFactors EC
entry.content:
Automating Employee Contract Extension by One Year Using Integration Centre in SAP SuccessFactors

Introduction

Managing employee contract extensions manually can be time-consuming for HR teams, especially when contracts expire on different dates.

In this blog, I will share an actual Integration Centre implementation that I configured in SAP SuccessFactors to automatically extend an employee's contract by one year when the defined business conditions are met.

The objective was simple:

If an employee is Active and their Contract End Date is today, automatically extend the Contract End Date by one year.

Business Requirement

The requirement was to automate the following scenario:

  • Employee Status = Active
  • Contract End Date = Today's Date
  • Automatically extend the Contract End Date by one year

Example

Field Before After
Employee StatusActiveActive
Contract End Date29-Sep-202629-Sep-2027

Instead of HR manually identifying employees whose contracts expire each day, the integration automatically identifies the eligible employees and updates their Job Information.

Solution Approach

I used Integration Centre with Job Information as both the source and target.

The overall process is:

Job Information
      ↓
Filter Active Employees
      ↓
Contract End Date = Today
      ↓
Calculate Contract End Date + 1 Year
      ↓
Update Job Information

This approach allows the process to be scheduled and executed automatically.

Step 1: Create the Integration

Navigate to:

Admin Centre → Integration Centre

Create a new integration using:

  • Source: Job Information
  • Target: Job Information

Select the required fields from Job Information that are needed for the update.

The integration reads the existing Job Information record and uses it to determine which employees need their contract extended.

Step 2: Configure the Field Mapping

The required Job Information fields are mapped from the source to the target.

The important fields include:

  • User ID to User ID 
  • Event Date to Contract End Date
  • Event Reason to Data Change or contact end date change (Default it)
  • Sequence Number to Sequence Number
  • Other mandatory Job Information fields required by the target configuration

Step 3: Calculate the New Contract End Date

This is the main part of the integration.

Instead of entering a fixed date, the integration calculates the new Contract End Date dynamically based on the employee's existing Contract End Date.

The logic is:

Existing Contract End Date
          +
       1 Year
          ↓
New Contract End Date

For example:

29-Sep-2026
     +
   1 Year
     ↓
29-Sep-2027

In Integration Centre, this is configured using Calculated Value for the Contract End Date field.

Actual expression used in the integration:
In the first drop down select fixed value =Today and use operand + 1 Years as shown below.

Note: Use the exact expression from the implemented integration here rather than a generic example. This is important because the calculation configuration is dependent on the actual Integration Center setup.

Step 4: Configure the Filters

The integration should not update every employee.

Therefore, I configured the integration to select employees only when both business conditions are satisfied.

Condition 1 – Employee Status

Employee Status = Active

Condition 2 – Contract End Date

Contract End Date = Today

Therefore, the effective selection criteria are:

Employee Status = Active
AND
Contract End Date = Today

This ensures that employees with future contract end dates are not processed prematurely.

Step 5: Update Job Information

Once an employee satisfies the filter conditions, the integration calculates the new Contract End Date and updates the employee's Job Information.

Example

Before Integration

Employee Status      : Active
Contract End Date    : 29-Sep-2026

After Integration

Employee Status      : Active
Contract End Date    : 29-Sep-2027

The employee's contract is therefore extended automatically by one year.

Step 6: Testing the Integration

Before scheduling the integration, I performed testing to validate the complete process.

The testing covered:

  1. Identifying an employee whose status was Active.
  2. Ensuring the employee's Contract End Date matched the processing date.
  3. Executing the integration.
  4. Verifying that the employee was picked up by the configured filters.
  5. Checking that the Contract End Date was extended by one year.
  6. Validating the updated record in Job Information.

This validation confirmed that the integration was updating the intended employees and applying the expected contract extension.

Step 7: Schedule the Integration

Once the integration was successfully tested, it can be scheduled to run daily.

A daily schedule ensures that employees whose contracts reach their end date are automatically identified without requiring HR to manually execute the process.

For example:

01-Oct-2026
Employee A → Contract End Date = Today → Extend by 1 Year

02-Oct-2026
Employee B → Contract End Date = Today → Extend by 1 Year

03-Oct-2026
Employee C → Contract End Date = Today → Extend by 1 Year

This provides a continuous automated process for contract extensions.

Important Considerations

1. Event Reason

The appropriate Event Reason should be configured according to the customer's business requirement and Job Information configuration. (In the above case I have defaulted to data change event reason)

The Event Reason is important because the update represents a change to the employee's Job Information.

2. Effective Date

The Effective Date and other required Job Information fields should be mapped correctly based on the target configuration.

Why Use Integration Center for This Requirement?

This approach provides several benefits:

  • Reduces manual HR effort
  • Eliminates the need to manually identify contracts expiring each day
  • Provides consistent processing
  • Allows the process to be scheduled
  • Uses existing Job Information data
  • Automatically calculates the new Contract End Date
  • Provides an auditable integration-based approach

End-to-End Flow

The complete implementation can be summarized as:

                 JOB INFORMATION
                       │
                       ▼
              Employee Status = Active
                       │
                       ▼
          Contract End Date = Today
                       │
                       ▼
        Calculate Contract End Date
                 + 1 Year
                       │
                       ▼
             Update Job Information
                       │
                       ▼
                Contract Extended

Conclusion

Using SAP SuccessFactors Integration Center, employee contract extensions can be automated based on business-defined conditions.

In this implementation, the integration checks whether an employee is Active and whether the Contract End Date is today. If both conditions are satisfied, the integration calculates a new Contract End Date by extending the existing date by one year and updates the employee's Job Information.

What would otherwise be a recurring manual HR activity can therefore be converted into a scheduled and automated process.

The key takeaway is that Integration Center can be used not only for data extraction but also for practical HR process automation when the right source, target, filters, calculations, and mappings are configured.

entry.title: 7,000 service specialists on one platform: What SAP IT Learned Scaling Enterprise Service Management
entry.content:
Yesterday, at SAP Connect, my colleague Natalia Emelianova - head of our SAP IT project team, shared the story and learnings of SAP's ESM global deployment to date. The transformation and approach are powerful and I want to share my perspective and key points from the session. 

The setup

Running shared services at enterprise scale is genuinely hard. With 110,000+ employees, 500,000+ customers, and operations spanning 157 countries, the complexity behind the scenes compounds quietly, year over year, until the tools you built for one version of the business are struggling to keep up with the next.

What it means at the business level

For operations, HR, and finance leaders, shared services has always been a lever for margin improvement. What we've seen as we've moved to SAP Enterprise Service Management is that when the platform is right, the efficiency gains tend to emerge across several dimensions at once: cycle times compress, cases resolve on first contact more often, and the volume of work that requires specialist intervention starts to shrink.

A 22-42% reduction in case cycle time and increased case deflection for HR services are meaningful indicators, but perhaps more telling is the 85% customer satisfaction score across the platform. When people find it easier to get what they need, the numbers tend to follow.

The ERP integration advantage

One of the things we've found most valuable, and something partners in this space understand well, is how much the native integration with the broader SAP landscape changes what's possible. Running ESM connected to SAP Business Suite, SAP Business AI, SAP Analytics Cloud, and Signavio-based process intelligence means the service layer is working from the same data that drives the business, rather than operating alongside it.

In SAP's Global Finance team, that's already translating into meaningful change across Order-to-Cash, Cash Collection, and Procurement processes. And as autonomous assistants come online for recurring receivables and dispute resolution, the integration becomes even more central allowing an AI-driven action to be grounded in real transaction context, not just a ticket summary.

The everyday experience

Beyond the business case, the more immediate impact is on the people doing the work every day. A finance team processing over 700,000 supplier invoices annually, or an HR organization managing 500,000 support tickets a year, experiences ESM differently than an executive reviewing a quarterly dashboard.

What we hear most from teams on the platform is that the work feels more manageable. Not only are the volume of cases reduced, but the cases that do come through are more complete. They arrive with context already gathered, routing is more accurate, and the tools they're using feel built for the complexity they're actually dealing with. That shift in day-to-day experience is harder to quantify but, in our view, equally important to the efficiency metrics.

Three starting points worth considering

For partners supporting customers through ESM implementations, and for organizations exploring what this kind of transformation could look like, these are the three principles that made the most difference in our own journey:

Process before platform. The technology is ready, but automating a process that isn't well-designed first tends to accelerate the wrong outcomes. Taking time to separate cases from service requests and redesign workflows before going live is where the real foundation gets built.

One line of business proves the model. Starting where the business pain is highest and stakeholder readiness is strongest creates a success story the rest of the organization can see. A phased approach isn't a slower path — it's a more reliable one.

Organizational change management is the implementation. User adoption is ultimately what determines whether the investment delivers. Teams that budget for OCM at the same level as the technical deployment consistently see better outcomes from the start.

In closing

We're grateful to everyone who joined the session and for the conversations that followed. The journey we shared is still in progress, and some of the most valuable thinking we've taken away from SAP Connect has come from partners and customers who are navigating similar challenges in their own organizations.

If you're working through any of these questions — whether you're early in an ESM evaluation or already mid-deployment — we'd genuinely welcome the conversation.

Thank you, @NataliaEmelianova, for providing your insights and delivering such a powerful session!

entry.title: Fixing the Orphaned Workflow Issue in SF Time Off Cancellation: withdrawWfRequest using Odata API
entry.content:
The Problem

If you're building a third-party integration either a mobile app, custom portal, or any external system that allows employees to request and cancel time off via SuccessFactors OData APIs, you may have run into this exact issue:

Employee cancels their time off request through your custom app. The EmployeeTime record correctly shows "approvalStatus = CANCELLED" in SF. But the manager still sees the request sitting in their approval inbox now showing a confusing "Cancelled" status that they can't do anything about, because the workflow instance itself was never terminated.

This is a common integration gap, and it happens because the business object and the workflow instance are two separate things in SF, and cancelling one does not automatically close the other.

This post demonstrates the full fix end-to-end, with real request/response payloads.

 

Why This Happens

Object What it represents
What updating it does
EmployeeTime recordThe actual time off data (dates, type, status)Changes the record's own status field only
WfRequest (workflow instance)The routing object sitting in the approver's inboxControls what the manager sees in their To-Do list

The EmployeeTime record and the WfRequest workflow instance are two separate objects in SF. Patching the record's approvalStatus field only changes the record itself it does not notify the workflow engine that the related approval item should close.

As a result, the workflow stays visible on the manager's screen even after the record shows CANCELLED, unless withdrawWfRequest is called explicitly to terminate that workflow instance.

 

The Full Flow: Demonstration

Step 1 - Employee cancels time off (existing working step) from Custom App

Below is the leave request detail Payload which be passed to CPI as request from custom application with Externalcode, User Id (LeaveRequestID), Time Type, Start Date and End Date

{
    "LeaveRequestID": "307eb8b817fd4e6c87f3d6ecdfc88cdf", --> External code of the leave
    "timeType": "1000",
    "userId": "test1",
    "startDate": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000",
    "endDate": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000"
}

Post Call: 

At this point, the time record is updated but the workflow is still active on the manager's screen. This is the gap.

Step 2 - Retrieve the associated wfRequestId

Before you can withdraw anything, you need the workflow ID tied to this specific time record. Query it via the navigation property or a filtered lookup:

GET call:

https://<api-server>/odata/v2/EmployeeTime?$select=externalCode,approvalStatus,endDate,startDate,timeType,userId,workflowRequestId&$filter=externalCode eq '${property.externalCode}' --> External code we got from mobile app ( in this case '307eb8b817fd4e6c87f3d6ecdfc88cdf')

Note: The exact navigation property name can differ depending on whether this is a standard object (EmployeeTime) or a custom MDF object . MDF objects typically expose this through a generic workflow association field configured in the object definition. Check your object's metadata ($metadata) if the property name above doesn't match your instance.

Step 3 - Withdraw the workflow (the actual fix)

Use the HTTP Adapter in CPI below screenshot to withdraw the workflow,

 

 

 

 

 


POST Call :
(use the worflow id from step 2) - https://<api-server>/odata/v2/withdrawWfRequest?wfRequestId=1937715L

API Response -

<d:WfRequestActionResponse>
 <d:element m:type="SFOData.WfRequestActionResponse">
<d:status>success</d:status>
<d:wfRequestId m:type="Edm.Int64">1937715L</d:wfRequestId>
 </d:element>
</d:WfRequestActionResponse>

The workflow instance is now terminated. It disappears from the manager's pending approvals, and the workflow history correctly reflects it as Withdrawn rather than leaving a dangling "Cancelled" item with no further action possible.

Pattern

Cancel object → Get wfRequestId → withdrawWfRequest (HTTP Adapter in CPI)

Applies to any standard or custom MDF object with workflow routing.


Error Handling:

 
Error CodeLikely Cause
COE_GENERAL_BAD_REQUESTEither the API user lacks withdrawWfRequest permission in WorkflowAllowedActionList, or the wfRequestId is invalid/already closed
404 on the wfRequestId lookupThe object may not have an active workflow (e.g., auto-approved request with no routing) — handle this gracefully and skip step 3
Permission error on withdrawConfirm this is a separate authorization from the one governing object creation/cancellation — easy to miss since the first two calls can work fine while this one fails

 

Summary

A clean cancellation flow for any workflow-routed object in SuccessFactors requires two actions, not one:

  1. Update the business object's status
  2. Explicitly withdraw the associated workflow instance via withdrawWfRequest

Skipping step 2 is what causes orphaned "Cancelled" items to linger on manager approval screens , a frustrating but entirely avoidable integration bug once you know the workflow engine and the business object are decoupled.

Hope you found this blog helpful, please leave your feedback or any suggestion in the comment. 

Thanks,
Amit

entry.title: SAP SuccessFactors Rollouts in SEA: Balancing Global Design with Local HR Requirements

SAP SuccessFactors Rollouts: What to Standardize Globally and What to Keep Country-Specific

I have had many opportunities to work on SAP SuccessFactors rollout projects, particularly across Asia. My scope has included Employee Central (EC) Core, Leave Management, Timesheets, Data Migration, Reports, and Role-Based Permissions (RBP).

In my previous blog, Lessons from a Phase 2 SAP SF Rollout: Governance, Migration Control, and Partner Accountability, I discussed project governance and migration control.

In this blog, I want to share my experience and recommendations from the HR and solution design perspective to make rollouts less complex and more hassle-free.

Let us get started!

1. Keep Your Foundation Design the Same

The first thing to consider during a rollout is how much of the existing foundation design can be retained.

In one of my implementations, we kept the organizational structure, including Business Unit, Division, and Department, consistent across countries. We only needed to collect country-specific data and upload it into the existing structure. This helped us retain a significant portion of the global design.

Adding an additional layer, such as a Group Business Unit for Southeast Asia, can still be accommodated without changing the overall structure.

2. Keep Your Job Structure Consistent

If the Job Code structure was designed logically during Phase 1, there is a good chance it can be retained during subsequent rollouts.

In my view, Job Codes can be structured around either of two possibilities

  • Job Function + Job Grade
  • Job Function + Job Family/Sub-Family + Job Grade

In our case, the second approach was the most suitable.

However, identifying Job Functions and Job Families can be challenging for clients migrating from SAP ECC or other legacy systems where these concepts were not formally established. This is where consulting expertise and an experienced HRIS team become important.

My recommendation: Start this exercise as early as possible. If the organization is doing it for the first time, begin with a pilot involving departments such as HR and Finance. Identify the relevant Job Functions, Families, and Roles, validate the approach, and then extend it to other departments. Delaying this exercise can potentially affect the project timeline.

3. Keep Your Pay Structure Consistent

Pay Components, Pay Grades, Pay Groups, and Pay Component Groups should follow the existing global design wherever possible.

Changes such as making fields mandatory, relabelling fields, or introducing custom fields should be aligned with global governance and followed by thorough testing to avoid unintended impacts on existing countries.

4. Keep HR Transaction Approval Processes Consistent

Another important factor in a successful rollout is harmonizing HR transaction approvals.

People and job titles may differ across countries, but the approval matrix should ideally be based on roles and responsibilities rather than specific job titles.

For example:

  • Probation: The L1 Manager manages the process, with L2 as approver. HR and the employee can be notified. Alerts can be configured at appropriate intervals before the probation end date.
  • Transfer: For Division or Department changes, the L1 Manager initiates the process, followed by the Releasing HOD and Receiving HOD, with HR involved where required.
  • Leave: Routine paid leave can generally be approved by the L1 Manager, while HR approval can be included for unpaid leave or applications exceeding a defined duration, depending on company policy.

In my rollout experience, we were broadly able to convince HR teams to retain consistent approval logic across countries. This resulted in better harmonization and a more consistent approach to HR transactions.

Of course, the final approval matrix must be validated against local policies, statutory requirements, and the organization's reporting structure.

5. Standardize Time Management, but Keep Policies Country-Specific

This is one of the most important areas during a rollout. Local statutory compliance can significantly influence the solution design. As consultants, we should understand these requirements before recommending standardization.

What Can Be Standardized?

Based on my experience, the following areas often provide opportunities for harmonization:

  1. Approval matrix and notifications: Maintain common approval workflows and email notifications wherever possible.
  2. Leave approvals: Reserve HR involvement for major or exceptional cases, reducing unnecessary administrative work.
  3. Leave reports: Use common reporting structures across countries.
  4. Non-statutory leaves: Marriage and compassionate leave may offer opportunities to standardize duration, eligibility, and approvals where local requirements permit.
  5. Timesheet design: Where appropriate, standardize the capture of working hours and overtime quantities, leaving monetary calculations to payroll.
  6. Payroll integration: Where supported by the receiving payroll system, transfer leave encashment as a pay component with the number of days. Paid and unpaid leave quantities can also be transferred in days, subject to the agreed integration design.

The objective is to minimize manual HR work and maintain a consistent solution without introducing unnecessary country-specific variations.

What Must Remain Country-Specific?

Overtime rates: Each country must follow its applicable statutory requirements. Organizations may offer more than the legal minimum where permitted, but they must not fall below the applicable requirements. A single global overtime rule is therefore not always appropriate.

Attendance and clock-in/clock-out requirements: Some countries have specific attendance recordkeeping requirements. Countries such as Japan and Brazil require careful assessment of the applicable rules and employee populations before deciding on the design.

Broadly, two approaches can be considered:

  • Option 1: Implement a clock-based timesheet design that captures the required attendance information.
  • Option 2: Retain the existing local system for attendance and overtime, integrating relevant leave and overtime data into SuccessFactors through a reverse feed where required.

In our case, we chose the second option. This allowed us to maintain a consolidated view in SuccessFactors without replacing a local system that already served the required purpose.

The decision should depend on compliance, integration feasibility, project scope, and the overall solution strategy.

Annual leave and statutory leave: Leave accrual, carry-forward, and seniority-based entitlements vary by country. These rules must be configured according to applicable local requirements rather than changed simply to achieve standardization. Specific leave types, such as national service leave, must also be supported where required.

The key lesson is that global design should provide a common framework, while local statutory rules determine the country-specific configuration.

6. Give Roles and Reports the Importance They Deserve

Roles and reports do not always receive sufficient attention during phased rollouts, even though they can create operational challenges later.

Country-Specific Roles

In our implementation, we created country-specific ESS roles, such as ESS (Malaysia) and ESS (Thailand), instead of relying exclusively on one role for every country.

This allowed each country's HR team to manage field visibility according to local requirements without unnecessarily affecting other countries. However, this flexibility should be balanced against the maintenance effort of creating too many roles.

Transactional vs. Strategic Reports

I followed the same principle for reporting.

Transactional reports, such as employee master data and leave data, can be adapted to country-specific operational needs.

Strategic reports, such as Headcount and Attrition, should ideally follow a common global design. This helps maintain consistent reporting definitions and enables meaningful comparisons across countries.

Conclusion:-

Based on my rollout experience, my recommendations are straightforward:

  1. Keep the foundation consistent. Retain organizational, job, and pay structures wherever possible.
  2. Keep approvals role-based. Harmonize approval logic across countries rather than designing it around individual job titles.
  3. Standardize where possible, but respect local compliance. Approval workflows, notifications, and reporting can often be harmonized, while overtime rates, leave accruals, and attendance requirements need country-specific consideration.
  4. Plan roles and reports early. Give local HR teams appropriate flexibility while retaining global consistency for strategic reporting.

Ultimately, a successful SAP SuccessFactors rollout is not about making every country identical. It is about identifying what can genuinely be standardized, understanding what must remain country-specific, and making those decisions early enough to avoid unnecessary complexity.

As consultants, our role is not simply to push for standardization. It is to understand the global template, recognize legitimate local differences, and recommend a solution that balances maintainability, business needs, and compliance.

Thank you for reading this blog! See you in the next one.🤗

Mohammad Saddam Aquib

entry.title: Peers, Reports & Team Size: The SuccessFactors Setup Guide
entry.content:
Introduction:

The latest People Profile can show a person’s peers, a manager’s direct reports, and team size right in the profile header. Here’s how to configure each one.

 Feature overview

On the Profile Preview and Full Profile header, users can select:

  • Peers: the peer count, opening a list with photos, display names, job title (or display title), and employment indicators
  • Direct reports and team size (on a manager’s profile): the same list view for the manager’s team

Depending on permissions, users can open each person’s Profile Preview and Full Profile.

Part 1: Configure Peers

Step 1: Enable the data model element
Enable the standard element teamMembersSize in the data model.

Step 2: Grant permissions

Give target roles permission to view the field. 

Employee Data -> Employee Profile

 

Step 3: Check the platform setting

Go to Admin Center > Platform Feature Settings and make sure Hide Peers is deactivated. It’s not enabled by default.

Part 2: Configure Direct Reports & Team Size

Step 1: Enable the data model elements
Enable both teamMembersSize and totalTeamSize.

Step 2: Grant permissions

Grant target roles “view” permission for both elements under the Employee Data > Employee Profile permission group.

 

Step 3: Enable the org chart

The org chart must be active for this feature to work.

Step 4: Grant navigation permission

Under User Permissions > General User Permission, grant the Organization Chart Navigation Permission to target roles.

You will be able to see the Count of Direct Reports , Peers and Team Size

⚠️ Configuration considerations

  • Multiple employments: peers, direct reports, and roles can differ per employment, and the data changes when users switch employments.
  • Contingent workers: included in team size and direct reports by default. To hide them for everyone, go to Company Settings > Org Chart Configuration and enable Hide Contingent Workers in Org Chart.
  • End-user org chart toggle: the “Include Contingent Workers” display setting does not affect team size and direct report calculations.
  • Inactive users: never included in team size or direct reports.
  • No peers: if a person has none, the Peers link doesn’t appear.
  • Multiple employments for direct reports: you can control whether they’re displayed through the global header search settings.

✅ Quick configuration checklist

☐ teamMembersSize enabled
☐ totalTeamSize enabled (for team size)
☐ View permissions granted to target roles
☐ Hide Peers deactivated
☐ Org chart enabled
☐ Organization Chart Navigation Permission granted

entry.title: Understanding the SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors Standard Product Connectors
entry.content:
If you are implementing SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors, one of the first things you need to understand is the set of standard product connectors that ship with the solution. These are not custom integrations. They are pre-built, productized connectors designed to keep data flowing between SAP SuccessFactors and SmartRecruiters automatically, consistently, and with SuccessFactors as the single source of truth.

This article walks through each connector, what it does, how it works, and what to watch out for during implementation.

1. SAP SuccessFactors User Sync

The User Sync is where everything starts. It automatically provisions and manages SmartRecruiters user accounts for employees maintained in SAP SuccessFactors, eliminating manual user creation and the overhead of maintaining accounts in two systems.

How it works

  • Automated provisioning: Access is controlled in SuccessFactors. User creation and permission maintenance happens there, and SmartRecruiters stays in sync.
  • Role and permission mapping: All active and inactive employees from SuccessFactors are synced to SmartRecruiters. Each user is created with an “Employee” role — system admins can update roles and permissions in SmartRecruiters as needed.
  • Deprovisioning and access control: When an employee is marked inactive or terminated in SuccessFactors, they are automatically marked as inactive in SmartRecruiters, maintaining security compliance.

All user data, including time zone, is managed from the user data file in SAP SuccessFactors.

Prerequisites

Core SuccessFactors setup must be completed before SmartRecruiters can be enabled and configured. This includes data models, foundation objects, picklists, languages, and permissions. If you are using Employee Central, its core data and features must also be configured prior to sync. Users must exist in the SuccessFactors platform before they can be synchronized.

Things to watch

Every user must have these mandatory attributes: Email, firstName, lastName, username, personUUID, and status. If any are missing, that individual user will not sync (the overall process continues for all other users).

A few important notes:

  • Duplicate email addresses within the same instance are not permitted — users sharing an email will not sync.
  • The same email address can exist across multiple instances (e.g. production and non-production).
  • The SmartRecruiters admin email (Main IT contact from provisioning) must be unique. Otherwise, the admin will lose access to the provisioned instance.

2. Synchronizing Job & Org Fields from SAP SuccessFactors

This is the Foundational Data Sync — and it is arguably the most important connector to get right. It connects SAP SuccessFactors master data to SmartRecruiters Job and Org fields, ensuring key organizational data is always accurate, consistent, and maintained from a single source of truth.

What gets synced

Data Type Examples

Foundation ObjectsLocation, Department, Division, Legal Entity, Cost Center
PicklistsAny standard or custom picklist defined in SAP SuccessFactors
Generic ObjectsCustom objects configured in the SuccessFactors platform
Dependencies / AssociationsParent-child field hierarchies are preserved
Values, Labels & TranslationsField values, labels, and translations are all carried across

How to set it up

The process uses the standard, pre-built field mapping tool in SAP SuccessFactors Admin Center:

  1. Identify which SmartRecruiters fields should be created using SuccessFactors data objects.
  2. Map SuccessFactors objects and picklists to SmartRecruiters Job or Org field categories.
  3. Initial sync creates the fields in SmartRecruiters and populates values from SuccessFactors.
  4. Scheduled jobs run automatically to keep values up to date.

In SmartRecruiters, these fields appear as read-only. Values cannot be edited directly — all changes must be made in SuccessFactors.

Dependencies and hierarchies

When objects with a parent-child relationship in SuccessFactors are selected during mapping, SmartRecruiters fields are created with the same dependency relationship. This keeps field hierarchy consistent across both systems.

Key points:

  • Parent-child relationships in SuccessFactors are reflected in SmartRecruiters as field dependencies.
  • Entire child field trees move together, preserving hierarchy.
  • A native SmartRecruiters field (e.g. Brand) can be set as the parent of a synced SuccessFactors field — allowing you to filter synced values based on a SmartRecruiters parent selection.
  • However, setting a SuccessFactors field as the parent of a SmartRecruiters field is not supported.

Things to watch

  • Changes to field values must be made in SuccessFactors, not SmartRecruiters.
  • Dependencies set during initial sync cannot be changed post-sync.
  • Field labels can be updated at any time via the mapping tool.
  • SmartRecruiters fields for recruitment-only data can still be created as standard single-select fields directly in SmartRecruiters.

SuccessFactors Foundational Data SyncSmartRecruiters view

3. Position to Job Creation from SAP SuccessFactors

The Position-to-Job connector enables authorized users to create a linked SmartRecruiters job directly from an approved position in the SuccessFactors Position Org Chart. The draft job is automatically pre-filled with position data.

The workflow

  1. Position approved — Position is created and approved in SuccessFactors Position Management.
  2. Job draft created — An authorized user triggers job creation from the Position Org Chart.
  3. Fields pre-populated — Job and Org fields are auto-filled from the position mapping configuration.
  4. Job published — The recruiter reviews, refines, and publishes the job in SmartRecruiters.

Supported field types for pre-population

  • Text fields created directly in SmartRecruiters
  • Single-select fields synced from SuccessFactors objects or picklists
  • Job Title, Position ID, Hiring Manager, and Coordinator (Originator) are mapped automatically
  • Supported SuccessFactors field types: String, Foundation Object, Generic Object, Picklist

Things to watch

  • Only active, visible, and non-transient position fields can be mapped.
  • Inactive or unmatched values are not pre-populated — fields will remain blank.
  • All pre-populated fields remain fully editable after the job draft is created.

4. Syncing Application Fields from SAP SuccessFactors

The Foundational Data Sync also extends to Application Fields — the fields that capture candidate-level data during the application process. The same principles apply: define and maintain data in SuccessFactors, and it automatically synchronizes to SmartRecruiters.

What gets synced

  • SuccessFactors objects and picklists: Any standard or custom picklist, generic object, or foundation object.
  • Application field categorization: Fields are created as Application Fields only.
  • Field values: Changes to object/picklist values in SuccessFactors are automatically reflected in SmartRecruiters.
  • en_US labels only: Field and value labels use the en_US locale. Other locales are not currently supported for application fields.

How to set it up

The process mirrors Job and Org field mapping:

  1. Identify which SmartRecruiters application fields should use SuccessFactors data objects.
  2. Map SuccessFactors objects/picklists to SmartRecruiters application fields, assigning a unique label per field.
  3. Initial sync creates the fields and populates values.
  4. Scheduled jobs keep values up to date automatically.

Why this matters for the hire flow

For picklist or object data to flow from SmartRecruiters Application Fields back into SAP SuccessFactors (during the hire process), the corresponding fields must be synchronized between the two systems. Fields should be created through the application sync process first — this enables accurate mapping from SmartRecruiters to SuccessFactors.

Things to watch

  • Changes to field values must be made in SuccessFactors, not SmartRecruiters.
  • Field labels can be updated at any time via the mapping tool.
  • SmartRecruiters application fields for recruitment-only data can still be created as standard single-select fields.
  • Fields can be synced multiple times and used for multiple fields, as long as each has a unique label.

Moving forward, if you want to leverage the full power of the integrated suite, all single select fields — whether Job, Org, or Application — must be created in SAP SuccessFactors and synchronized to SmartRecruiters via Foundational Data Sync.

This is crucial to support:

  • Position to Job integration
  • Integration to Onboarding
  • Business Rules integration (Roadmap item)
  • Translations (Roadmap item)

This does not mean every single select field needs to follow this approach. But if any of the above capabilities are in scope for your implementation, creating fields directly in SmartRecruiters is not an option for those fields.

Bottom line: Plan your field strategy early. If there is any chance a field will be involved in position mapping, onboarding data transfer, business rules, or multi-language support, create it in SuccessFactors first and sync it across.

5. Sending Hires from SmartRecruiters to SAP SuccessFactors

The Hire Sync streamlines the hiring process by automatically transferring candidate and job-related data from SmartRecruiters to SAP SuccessFactors, supporting both new hires and internal transfers. This reduces manual data entry, minimizes errors, and accelerates onboarding.

How it works

  1. Sync foundational data — Use the Set Up SmartRecruiters Field Mapping tool in Admin Center to sync SuccessFactors foundational data to SmartRecruiters.
  2. Configure field mapping — Map SmartRecruiters job and application fields to SuccessFactors Employee Central fields via the Integration Hub.
  3. Initiate hire in SmartRecruiters — Triggering the hiring action advances the candidate to the Hired step, logs the activity, and initiates the transfer of candidate data to SuccessFactors.
  4. Data transferred on hire — Candidate data is automatically transferred to Employee Central and/or Onboarding.

Mapping details

Mapping Type Details

Auto-mapped fieldsStart Date, Hiring Manager, Position ID, Legal Entity
Mandatory field mappingFirst Name, Last Name, Email (required for successful hire transfer)
Event Reason configurationConfigurable for Transfer and Hire event types, or defaulted automatically
Available candidate dataPersonal Information, Employment Details, Job Information, Email & Phone

Pre-population of candidate data is driven by field mapping configured in the SmartRecruiters to Employee Central Integration Hub. The same mapping applies to both Employee Central and Onboarding, as well as internal and external hires.

6. Career Site Builder for SmartRecruiters

Career Site Builder (CSB) is available today and provides the branded career site experience for SmartRecruiters. Current capabilities include:

  • Core CSB functionality for building and managing career sites
  • Internal career site powered by CSB
  • Single ATS mode (SmartRecruiters only)
  • Dual ATS mode (SmartRecruiters + SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting running concurrently)
  • Winston Chat in single ATS mode
  • Advanced Analytics in dual ATS mode (data shown up to Apply Start)

Bringing It All Together

These six standard product connectors form the backbone of the SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors integration. They are designed to work together as a connected set:

  1. User Sync ensures the right people have access.
  2. Foundational Data Sync (Job/Org) establishes the shared organizational data layer.
  3. Position to Job connects workforce planning to recruitment execution.
  4. Application Field Sync extends shared data into the candidate experience.
  5. Hire Sync closes the loop by sending new hires back to Employee Central and Onboarding.
  6. Career Site Builder provides the external and internal candidate-facing experience.

The key takeaway for implementation teams: start with the foundations. Get your data models, picklists, and foundation objects right in SuccessFactors first. Then let the standard connectors do their job. The more you lean into SuccessFactors as the single source of truth, the smoother your integration will be — and the more capabilities you will be able to unlock down the line.

entry.title: From Generation to Governance: What’s New in Document Generation (2H 2026)
entry.content:
Introduction of Document Generation Usage Record :

Until now, there was no built-in way to see when a document was generated in Employee Central.

What’s new

Every successful document generation now creates a record in the new Document Generation Usage Record MDF object. This applies to all Document Generation Templates and categories.

Each record captures:

  • The template used
  • The source of initiation
  • The target user
  • The output type
  • Applicable signature requirements
  • Other relevant details

Why it matters

  • Traceability: one consistent trail of generation activity across modules
  • Reporting: a reliable data source for usage and audit reporting
  • Efficiency: no more manual checks to find out what was generated, when, and for whom

How to get started

The records are created automatically, so there is nothing to switch on. To view them:

  1. Grant access. Go to User Permissions → Document Generation Object Permissions → Document Generation Usage Record and select the permissions each role needs.
  2. View the records. Open Manage Data and select the Document Generation Usage Record object.

This is one of the most exciting and the much-awaited features that was long requested and finally its live in the 2H 2026 Release.

Workflow Approval for Document Generation in Employee Central

Until now, a generated document went straight to its recipient. For sensitive or legal documents, there was no way to check correctness, compliance, or timing first.

2H 2026 Release adds workflow approval to Document Generation, so documents are reviewed and approved before they are sent.

What’s new

You can assign a workflow to a Document Generation template. When a document is generated from a workflow-enabled template, the system:

  1. Creates a Document Generation Usage Record
  2. Uploads the document to Document Management Service (DMS)
  3. Triggers the approval workflow

Approvers can review both the generated document and its generation details before approving or rejecting. The document is emailed to the recipient only after approval is complete.

Why the workflow runs on the usage record, not the template: the usage record represents one specific generation instance, including the template, the generated document, the recipient, and the user who generated it. That is what an approver needs to see.

Good to know

  • Workflows can be configured only for storage-enabled templates.
  • The feature supports only templates in the Document Generation category.
  • The workflow must already exist before you configure the template.

How to set it up

  1. Enable storage. In the Document Generation template, assign a custom DMS document category to the Generated Document Storage Category field.

    Creation of CustomDMSCategory

    Manage Documents -> Create a New Category


    Document Generation Template :

     

  2. Assign the workflow. Select the workflow in the Assign Workflow For Generation field.
  3. Create a rule. Use the Trigger Workflows rule scenario with Document Generation Usage Record as the base object. Derive the workflow from Document Generation Usage Record → Document Generation Template → Assign Workflow For Generation.

  4. Attach the rule. In Configure Object Definition, open the Document Generation Usage Record MDF object, assign the rule under Save Rules, and save.



  5. If a workflow enabled template is tried to be downloaded direct , we will get a error popup which states the following  , however this can be by-passed when downloaded from the Generate Document UI (However we need to set it to Yes for Store-Generated Documents)

    Take Action UI :



    Generate Document UI :





Store Generated HR Documents in DMS: Document Generation Meets Document Management Service

Until now, generated documents weren’t stored automatically in Document Management Service (DMS). Keeping a controlled copy meant extra manual handling by HR.

This release changes that. Documents generated from templates in the Document Generation category can now be stored in SAP SuccessFactors DMS under a custom document category.

For the documents to be stored in the custom category , The Category needs to be assigned to the Document Generation Template.

entry.title: Automating Referral Bonus Payouts: RCM to EC
entry.content:
Introduction & Business Problem

Employee referral programs are among the most effective recruitment channels for organizations. However, managing the end-to-end operational lifecycle from tracking candidate referrals in Recruiting Management (RCM) to paying out referral bonuses in Employee Central (EC) often involves significant manual administration.

In a standard setup:

  • Referrals are captured within Recruiting Management (RCM).
  • The candidate is hired.
  • HR or payroll teams manually pull reports, calculate milestone eligibility (e.g., 3 months post-hire, passed probation etc), and import spreadsheets into Employee Central (EC) as non-recurring payments.

This manual handover creates operational bottlenecks, delayed payouts, and tracking discrepancies.

In this blog, we walk through an end-to-end, and fully automated solution that bridges the gap between RCM and EC using Custom Metadata Framework (MDF) Objects, Associations, and Integration Center jobs eliminating external middleware and manual imports. 

High-Level Solution Architecture

Step-by-Step Implementation

Step 1: Define Referral Amount and Payment Date Logic

Before configuring the integration, decide how your organization determines bonus amounts and payout timing. 

  • Where should the Referral Amount live?

    Job Requisitions include a standard referral bonus field. If your payout is tied to the position/hiring country, keeping it on the requisition template is the easiest way to track and adjust values per role. However, if your payout is based on the referrer's country, you don't need it on the requisition you can calculate it on the fly using a business rule or integration logic.

  • When should the bonus be paid?

    Payment timing is fully flexible. Depending on your business policy, it can be scheduled immediately after the candidate finishes probation, based on a fixed timeline (such as 3 or 6 months after the hire date), or customized by region.

 

Step 2: Configure Custom MDF Tracking Objects

To handle one referrer referring multiple applicants, configure a Parent-Child (Composite) MDF relationship under Configure Object Definitions:

Navigate to Configure Object Definition -- Create New -- Object Definition.

1. Parent Object: cust_ParentReferralTracking

2. Child Object: cust_ChildReferralTracking

Create Child object and add required fields

 

Associate the child object with parent object

 

Step 3: Create Pay Component

Navigate to Manage Organisation, Pay and Job Structures and create a non recurring pay component to capture Referral Amount in EC.

Step 4: Add MDF Object on employee profile.

Navigate to Manage Configuration UI - Create New -- Select Parent Referral Object. Update the required fields, labels, UI etc and Save.

Navigate to Configure Latest People Profile, Add Category, add the Object and save it.

This will add a card on employee profile which provide all referral information.

Step 5: Grant Permissions

Navigate to Manage Permission Roles to provide appropriate access to the newly created MDF objects and pay component and the employee referral card created.

Step 6: Build Integration Center Job 1 (RCM to Custom MDF)

This job extracts referral details for successfully hired candidates and stages them in our custom MDF.

  • Source Starting Entity: CandidateEmployeeReferral.

  • Target Entities: cust_ParentReferralTracking and composite child cust_ChildReferralTracking.

Map the fields correctly and add a filter on candidate status, that only Hired candidates should be considered and referred one.

 

Step 7: Build Integration Center Job 2 (MDF to One-Time Payment)

This scheduled integration evaluates records in the custom tracking object and creates spot bonus payouts in EC.

  • Source Starting Entity: cust_ChildReferralTracking.

  • Target Entity: EmpPayCompNonRecurring (Spot Bonus)

Step 8: Job Scheduling & Sequencing

To ensure data integrity, schedule the two Integration Center jobs in sequential order with a buffer of at least 2 to 3 hours:

  • First Job (RCM -- MDF): Populates and updates the custom referral tracking records.
  • Second Job (MDF -- EC): Triggers a few hours later to read the updated MDF data and create the one-time payments.

Below are previews of how the data looks once the solution is running end-to-end.


Key Advantages of This Design

  • Full Operational Transparency: HR administrators and managers can view referral progression directly on MDF portlets without querying recruitment pipelines.
  • Zero Middleware Dependency: Accomplished 100% natively within SAP SuccessFactors using standard Integration Center capabilities—no external middleware (SAP Integration Suite / CPI) licenses required.
  • Audit Trail: Because notes and job requisition IDs are linked into EmpPayCompNonRecurring,  payroll and compensation teams maintain complete visibility into payment origins.
  • Employees gain transparency into referral progress directly on their People Profile.

Conclusion

Connecting Recruiting Management to Employee Central using MDF objects and Integration Center turns a manual, error-prone spreadsheet routine into a seamless automated process. Best of all, this solution requires zero external middleware or extra licensing, running 100% within SAP SuccessFactors.

Thanks for reading! Have you implemented a similar setup, or do you handle milestone payouts differently? Share your thoughts, questions, or feedback in the comments below.

Happy optimizing and happy learning! 🙂

entry.title: Second Half 2026 Release: Enabling Frictionless People Operations with Agentic AI
entry.content:
HR teams today are expected to move faster than ever while managing increasingly complex workforce operations. From maintaining accurate workforce data and processing employee changes to managing approvals, time, benefits, and payroll-related activities, operational excellence has become a critical component of business success. Yet many organizations still spend valuable time navigating manual processes, resolving data issues, and overcoming workflow bottlenecks that slow productivity and impact employee experiences. 

As organizations continue their journey toward Autonomous HCM, reducing operational friction is becoming increasingly important. By leveraging agentic AI, organizations can proactively identify issues, automate routine work, and keep critical processes moving, allowing employees, managers, and HR teams to focus on work that matters most.

With the SAP SuccessFactors HCM second half 2026 release, we're introducing new innovations designed to enable frictionless people operations. From intelligent HR administration and workforce management to streamlined benefits administration and system management, these capabilities help organizations reduce manual effort, prevent errors, and improve operational efficiency across the employee lifecycle.

HR Operations Assistant: Transforming HR Administration with Agentic AI

HR teams spend a significant amount of time managing employee changes, resolving data inconsistencies, monitoring workflows, and maintaining accurate workforce records. While these activities are critical to business operations, they can also create bottlenecks, increase manual effort, and introduce risk when issues go undetected.

The HR Operations Assistant helps streamline people operations while improving data accuracy, service delivery, and workforce agility at scale. Designed to reduce friction across the HR lifecycle, the assistant proactively identifies and resolves data issues, streamlines employment and organizational changes, accelerates workflows, optimizes position management, and helps safeguard payroll-related transactions.

Working behind the scenes, AI-powered capabilities continuously monitor employee, job, position, and payroll-related data for inconsistencies, surfacing issues with contextual insights and guided resolution steps before they impact downstream processes. By helping organizations identify and address issues earlier, HR teams can improve data quality, reduce manual effort, and operate with greater confidence. 

The assistant also streamlines employee and organizational changes by identifying required information, predicting values, and automatically populating fields to simplify administrative tasks. entry.title: Compliance Forms in Employee Central - All you need to know!
entry.content:
Introduction:

Until this release, compliance forms in SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding were exclusively available as part of the onboarding journey. Once an employee transitioned to active status in Employee Central, there was no supported, native mechanism to trigger or re-complete those forms without initiating a new onboarding process. Customers managing cross-border assignments, state or location changes, or periodic regulatory re-compliance requirements had no choice but to handle forms outside the platform — through email, manual PDF workflows, or standalone compliance tools.

With this Release, active EC employees (with or without Onboarding Process) can now generate and complete legally mandated compliance forms directly from their People Profile at any point during the employee lifecycle — using the same forms, configurations, and screens already in place from onboarding, with no duplicate setup required.

What Has Changed:

 Previous BehaviourNew Behaviour
Compliance form accessOnboarding journey only — active EC employees had no self-service pathActive EC employees can trigger compliance forms directly from their People Profile via "Generate Compliance Forms"
Country eligibilityHardcoded to Canada only at the EC integration layerNow, it is supported for Canada and the United States via Employee Profile
Form configuration reuseN/A — separate tooling needed for post-onboarding complianceSame ONB forms, configurations, and screens reused — no duplicate setup
Country determinationN/AWork Location country → Legal Entity country → Home Address country (precedence order)
Digital signatureN/ADocuSign available after form completion; signed documents stored in DMS
Document storageN/ASigned documents stored in DMS and visible in the Documents section of the Latest People Profile

Prerequisites:

Before beginning configuration, confirm all of the following:
  • Both Onboarding 2.0 and Employee Central are active and integrated in the same environment.
  • Compliance forms are already configured in Onboarding by country and/or state, with correct mappings to Work Location and Legal Entity hierarchies. 

Configuration: Step-by-Step

  1. Admin Center → Compliance Settings → [Select Country] → [Select Compliance Form Category] → Add New Configuration → Enable: "Enable Accessibility of Compliance Forms in Employee Central"
  2. Admin Center → Manage Permission Roles → [Relevant role] → User Permissions → Compliance Object Permissions → Enable: ComplianceFormGroupConfiguration
  3. Admin Center → Manage Permission Roles → [Relevant role] → User Permissions → Compliance Object Permissions → Grant All Compliance Permissions
  4. Admin Center → Manage Permission Roles → [Employee / relevant role] → Onboarding or Offboarding Permissions → [Relevant compliance form task permissions] → Grant access

Refer to the relevant documentation at the bottom of the blog.

Employee-Facing Flow:

  1. Employee navigates to their People Profile in Employee Central.
  2. Under "Take Action" (Legacy People Profile) or "All Actions" (Latest People Profile), the employee selects "Generate Compliance Forms".
  3. The system checks for any ongoing compliance process. If one exists, a new one is not triggered.
  4. A pop-up appears showing the countries resolved from the employee's Job Information (Work Location → Legal Entity → Home Address precedence).
  5. For employees with multiple concurrent employments or global assignments, all applicable countries are shown. The employee selects the country or countries for which they want to complete forms.
  6. For each selected country, the applicable compliance forms are displayed:
    • Mandatory forms are pre-selected and cannot be deselected.
    • Optional forms display a Skip option.
  7. The employee clicks "Generate Forms" — a ToDo is created with the selected forms attached to a dedicated compliance engagement card.
  8. A success confirmation pop-up appears. The ToDo appears on the employee's Home Page.
  9. The employee opens the ToDo and accesses forms through the dedicated compliance engagement card (separate from general ONB tasks).
  10. Forms are rendered using ONB screens. If direct screen reuse is not feasible for a specific form type, a legacy screen fallback is used automatically with full functional parity.
  11. After completing all forms, the employee can initiate a compliance e-signature.
  12. Signature status flows back to the ToDo and form records. Signed documents are stored in DMS and appear in the Documents section of the Latest People Profile.

Troubleshooting Guide

Issue 1: "Generate Compliance Forms" action does not appear in EC Actions

Resolution steps:
  1. Verify Admin Center → Compliance Settings is enabled for the relevant country and form category.
  2. Check whether the employee has active Job Information with a valid country resolution (Work Location, Legal Entity, or Home Address). If no country can be determined, the action may be suppressed.

Issue 2: The country pop-up appears but shows no countries

Resolution steps:
  1. Navigate to Admin Center → Manage Data → ComplianceFormGroupConfiguration → Forms associated with the country are present
  2. Verify the "Enable Accessibility of Compliance Forms in Employee Central" checkbox is enabled in Compliance Settings for the relevant country and form category.
  3. Confirm the employee's Job Information has a correctly populated Work Location with a country value, a Legal Entity with a location country, or a valid Home Address country.

 Issue 3: ToDo is not created after clicking "Generate Forms"

Resolution steps:
  1. Check whether an error message appears in the pop-up after clicking "Generate Forms".
  2. Validate the error and resolve this, only after the error is resolved, the ToDo is created.

Issue 4: Employee cannot access the forms from the ToDo compliance engagement card

Resolution steps:
  1. Check the employee's Onboarding permission role — they must have permissions to complete compliance form tasks and access the specific form screen.
  2. Verify the employee is within their own target population for the Onboarding compliance permission roles in self-service scenarios.

Issue 5: When using Docusign, the DocuSign signature prompt does not appear after form completion

Resolution steps:
  1. Verify DocuSign is enabled and the integration endpoint is reachable.
  2. Confirm the specific compliance form type is configured to require a digital signature in ONB Compliance Form Settings. Not all forms trigger DocuSign.

Issue 6: Completed form does not appear in the employee's documents

Resolution steps:
  1. Confirm the employee is checking the Documents section of their Latest People Profile — this is where EC-initiated compliance documents are stored.
  2. If the form should appear in EC document views but does not, check DMS storage permissions and the document category configuration for EC compliance form storage.
